captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Consensus pick across all channels. Mercedes still the benchmark car despite Barcelona loss. DNF in Barcelona was mechanical, not performance-related. Still the highest-ceiling 2x asset despite DNF hurting his trailing average. Multiple sources explicitly say do NOT sell Antonelli.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lewis Hamilton
captains.reason: Won Barcelona with 56 fantasy points — his best in 4+ years. P2-P2-P1 in last three races. Only driver alongside Gasly to score championship points every race weekend. Ferrari bringing engine update. FormulaFantasyHub calls him 'in a class of his own' right now. ZachGP considers him a viable 2x alternative to Antonelli.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: At price floor — literally cannot lose budget. 82% ownership in global top 500. Must-have budget enabler per all sources. Consensus must-own. Needs 21 points for 0.2 rise (unlikely this week), but zero downside risk. DNF in Barcelona was freak gravel incident, not reliability.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Strong consensus pick across ZachGP, F1FantasyPolePosition, and ReinFantasy. Needs only -12 for min price rise, -7 for max rise — virtually guaranteed budget increase. 28 points over last 2 races (14/race avg). Racing Bulls car looking competitive. Preferred over Bortoleto for budget building.

buy.name: Pierre Gasly
buy.note: Six double-digit scores in last seven races. Hasn't scored below double digits this season except Miami (taken out by Lawson). Highest average points of any B-tier driver. Needs -9 for 0.2 rise, 2 points for max rise — near-guaranteed price increase. Robbed of 0.8M from Monaco points adjustment. Essential if budget allows.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: P6 or higher in three straight races. 22 points in Barcelona (2nd-highest fantasy score of career). Needs -8 for min rise, 3 for max rise. Very close to Gasly in stats. Multiple sources see Gasly vs Hadjar as the key B-tier debate — both are strong, pick based on budget needs.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Fine hold if already owned. Double-digit points in 3 of last 4 races. Needs 2 points for min rise, 10 for max. Not worth a transfer to bring in over Gasly/Hadjar, but no urgency to sell.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: Very consistent floor (7-5-5-7 recent scores) but limited upside for max price rise. 71% top-500 ownership. Fine hold but Lindblad preferred for budget building. F1FantasyPolePosition says going Bortoleto → Lindblad saves 0.2M and has better price rise outlook.

consider.name: Esteban Ocon
consider.note: Only 8 points needed for 0.2 rise. Fine to hold if you lack transfers to move him out. Not worth actively buying — prioritize Gasly/Hadjar/Lindblad transfers first.

avoid: Valtteri Bottas — 3.3M but Cadillac reliability is dreadful. Expected another DNF. Only hold if no transfers available or extreme budget building for 4A.
Sergio Perez — 6.2M is more expensive than Lindblad/Bortoleto with worse upside. Cadillac reliability concerns. DNF regression likely. Best top-500 teams have zero Cadillac/Aston Martin exposure.
Franco Colapinto — Monaco zero hangs on his rolling average making him a poor long-term hold. Transfer out to fund Hulkenberg or Lindblad.
Lance Stroll — Falling in price, Aston Martin not competitive enough.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: Multiple sources point to Silverstone (sprint weekend, next race) as a much better wildcard target. Austria is about positioning and budget building for the 4A transition, not chip usage. ReinFantasy explicitly frames Austria as setup for the more important Silverstone deadline.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: F1FantasyPolePosition explicitly says wouldn't play limitless here. While 4 straight mode zones offer overtakes, it's a standard race weekend with no sprint. Save for a sprint weekend or higher-variance event.

watch_items: Ferrari engine update: Multiple sources mention Ferrari bringing a significant engine upgrade. Watch FP1-FP3 to see if it closes the gap to Mercedes or boosts customer teams (Haas/Racing Bulls).

Extreme heat (34°C): Mercedes historically struggled with cooling in high temps in the 2022-2025 era. Watch if Mercedes has to turn down engine modes, which could impact Antonelli/Mercedes constructor scoring.
Red Bull engine update impact on Racing Bulls and Hadjar/Lindblad/Lawson — could reshuffle midfield pecking order.
Cadillac reliability over 71 laps in extreme heat — key for Bottas/Perez owners deciding whether to hold or sell.
Monaco appeals still ongoing: McLaren and Red Bull challenging Gasly's reinstatement. If overturned, could trigger another points/price adjustment (though F1 Fantasy said no backdated adjustments).

4A lineup viability: Track your budget carefully. With Hulkenberg at 3M floor and assets dropping, the 4A build (2 premium drivers + 2 premium constructors) may become achievable at Silverstone. Use Austria transfers to set up budget for this transition.
FP1/FP2/FP3 data: Three practice sessions available. Use Friday and Saturday data to finalize team — especially for Audi cooling concerns and Ferrari upgrade assessment.
arc: Austria is explicitly framed by multiple sources as a setup race for the more consequential Silverstone sprint weekend double-header. The key strategic arc is the transition from 3A lineups (1 premium driver + 2 premium constructors) to 4A lineups (2 premium drivers + 2 premium constructors), which is on the cusp of affordability. Budget building is paramount — hence the consensus around price-floor Hulkenberg, near-guaranteed-riser Lindblad, and the Gasly/Hadjar B-tier picks. ReinFantasy notes that top teams are approaching 117-118M in budget and the 4A threshold could be hit at Silverstone if budget is managed well in Austria. Additionally, Ferrari's engine update and the extreme Austrian heat could reveal whether Ferrari has genuinely closed the gap to Mercedes or whether Barcelona was a one-off, which will determine whether Hamilton becomes a must-have 2x option or remains a strong differential alongside Antonelli through the European summer swing.
